paper.title: Sovereign AI Architecture for Distribution Loss and Theft Reduction in Pakistan

scenario: the operator is described by class, never by name: an electricity distribution company in Pakistan serving several million customers through hundreds of grid stations and thousands of feeders, with the first phase on one circle of feeders for one quarter, reading seven systems of record through one adapter family and writing back only approved corrections and approved theft cases
source: chapter 5 of the paper (the fifteen objects in 5.1, the draft and approval vocabularies in 5.2, the Grid station record in 5.3), the properties and the fourteen labelled typed links of Figure 4, and the anchors and links of Table 8; the Recovery anchor follows chapter 2.1 (the theft case register holds recovery amounts); Agent draft and Approval are the platform's own decision record (5.2) and carry no system of record, so their anchor is left empty; properties the figure truncates are left out.

write_paths: the adapter tier (one integration adapter family: a Kafka subscription for meter data, scheduled batch extracts for billing, energy audit, GIS and outage records, mapped connectors for the field app and the theft case register), stamping every fact with the system it came from

the approved correction, the single write path out of the platform: reading and multiplier corrections land in the customer information and billing system and approved theft cases land in the theft case register, each through the adapter tier and each traceable to the approval object that authorized it

the surfaces used by named subdivision engineers, inspection officers and revenue officers (identity held by Keycloak inside the boundary): the approval queue and loss boards, the case file queue, the correction queue, the printable complaint pack and the command center
human_loop: agents draft and people decide: the loss agent's ranked causes and inspection visits are approved by the subdivision engineer, the tamper agent's case file by the inspection officer, the billing agent's correction by the revenue officer, and the theft complaint is signed by the Grade 17 officer; no agent disconnects a customer, raises a bill or files a case without a recorded approval carrying an artifact hash and a written reason
